DEVELOPING CONVERSATIONS
Apparently
We often introduce sentences about things in the
news with apparently. This shows we are not 100%
certain these facts are true - we are just reporting
what we have heard.
Apparently, she found out her husband was having
an affair with another Hollywood actress.
Apparently, they think his attackers might have been
even younger than him.

PRONUNCIATION Responding to news
When we comment on things people tell us, we
often add the question tags wasn't it? / isn't it?
As we expect people to agree with us in these
situations, our voice goes down on the tag.
E: Did you see that thing on TV about the murder
last night?
F: Yeah, It was shocking, wasn't it?
